Byomkesh Bakshi.description: The protagonist and 'truth seeker' (satyanweshi), a detective known for his logical and practical approach to mysteries.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, often assisting in investigations and narrating the stories.

Mr. Vishu Vinayak Apte.description: A Maharashtrian police official who befriends Byomkesh and introduces him to Poona and Mahabaleshwar.

Shorab Homji.description: The Parsi owner of Shayahadri Hotel in Mahabaleshwar, previously a regular guest and now a key informant in the case.

Manek Mehta.description: A Gujarati businessman with a criminal background, initially believed to be the murderer but later revealed as the victim.

Bijoy Biswas.description: A Bengali hotelier and partner to Mehta who disguises himself as the servant Mahesh at Haimabati's house to conceal his involvement in a murder conspiracy.

Haimabati.description: Bijoy Biswas's wife, described as attractive and dignified, later revealed to be complicit in the murder.

Bikash Dutta.description: Ajit and Byomkesh's assistant, who helps Ajit during the investigation in Calcutta.

Shailarahasya.description: The Bengali title of the story, meaning 'The Phantom Client' or 'The Mystery of the Phantom'.

Shayahadri Hotel.description: A hotel in Mahabaleshwar, central to the story's events.

Mahabaleshwar.description: A hill station in Maharashtra, known for its scenic beauty and as the main setting of the mystery.

Pune.description: A major city in Maharashtra, also referred to as Poona, visited by Byomkesh.

Bombay.description: Now known as Mumbai, a major Indian city where Byomkesh completes some work.

Singh Garh.description: A historic fort near Pune, also known as Sinhagad.

Bhabani Mandir.description: A temple mentioned as a tourist site in Poona.

Western Ghats.description: A mountain range in western India, through which Byomkesh travels.

Darjeeling.description: A famous hill station in West Bengal, compared to Mahabaleshwar in the story.

Maharastra.description: The Indian state where much of the story takes place, including Mahabaleshwar and Pune.

Goa.description: A coastal state in western India, mentioned as one of Mehta's residences.

Ahmedabad.description: A major city in Gujarat, India, where Bijoy and Haimabati previously ran a hotel.

Pakistan.description: A neighboring country, referenced in connection with gold smuggling.

Calcutta.description: Now Kolkata, a major city in West Bengal and home to Byomkesh and Ajit.

Faridpur.description: A district in East Bengal (now Bangladesh), the servant Mahesh's place of origin.

East Bengal.description: A region now part of Bangladesh, referenced for Mahesh's background.

Pratap Ghar Fort.description: A historic fort near Mahabaleshwar, also known as Pratapgad.

Bombay Point.description: A popular sunset point in Mahabaleshwar.

saree.description: A traditional Indian garment worn by women, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

vermilion.description: A red powder (sindoor) traditionally applied by married Hindu women in the parting of their hair.
